title: C# Questions & Answers - Constructors in Class
sourceFile: Class Constructors - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on constructors in class in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: How many constructors can a class define in C#?
questions.explanation: A class can define any number of constructors as long as their signatures (parameter lists) are different. This is known as constructor overloading.

questions.question: Choose the correct way of defining constructors for the 'maths' class to support the following initializations:
questions.code:
maths s1 = new maths();
maths s2 = new maths(5, 5.4f);

options.text: public maths(int pp, float tt) { p = pp; t = tt; }

public maths() { p = 0; t = 0.0f; }
public maths(int pp, float tt) { p = pp; t = tt; }

questions.explanation: Since the code initializes one object with no parameters and another with two parameters, the class must define both a default constructor and a parameterized constructor.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to initialize an object for the class 'abc' defined below?
questions.explanation: The object initialization must match the constructor's signature, which requires an 'int' followed by a 'float'.

questions.question: Which statement about constructors in C# is correct?

options.text: Constructors are called implicitly when an object is created via 'new'
Constructors have the same name as the class

questions.explanation: Constructors share the class name, can be overloaded with different parameters, and are automatically executed when an instance of the class is created.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a constructor?
questions.explanation: The main role of a constructor is to initialize the fields/properties of an object when it is first created.

questions.question: Can the method add() be overloaded in C# as shown below?
questions.code:
public int add() { /*...*/ }
public float add() { /*...*/ }
questions.explanation: In C#, methods cannot be overloaded based solely on their return types. The parameter list must be different.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about constructors in C#?

options.text: A constructor cannot be declared as private
A class can have a static constructor

questions.explanation: C# supports static constructors which are used to initialize static data or perform a particular action that needs to be performed only once.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: second method, 20, second method, first method
first method, 20, first method, second method

questions.explanation: 1. abc.a() prints 'first method'. 2. k.b(20) prints '20', then calls b(). 3. b() calls a() which prints 'first method', then prints 'second method'.

questions.question: What is the return type of a constructor in C#?
questions.explanation: Constructors do not have a return type, not even 'void'.

questions.question: Which special method is used to initialize an object and has the same name as its class?
questions.explanation: By definition, a constructor is a special member function of a class that is executed whenever we create new objects of that class.
